experiments.title: Seedfall
experiments.idea: Seedfall: walk a moonlit orchard floor and nudge glowing seeds into their hollows, one new idea per glade

experiments.title: Nightbloom
experiments.idea: Nightbloom: open a night meadow of flowers with one thumb - tap a flower and it opens along with its neighbours, one new flower kind per level.

experiments.title: Summerkeep
experiments.idea: Summerkeep: sort jars of preserved summer berries onto their own shelves, one new rule at a time

experiments.title: Deeproot
experiments.idea: Deeproot: grow a sapling root down through the earth toward a buried ember, one rule at a time

experiments.title: Moonmirror Marsh
experiments.idea: Moonmirror Marsh: a calm pixel-art night marsh where you rotate stone mirrors so a moonbeam reaches every reed-lantern, one new rule per level.

experiments.title: Lantern Ice
experiments.idea: A moonlit frozen lake you cross with one thumb: tap a direction and the little lantern-keeper skids over the ice until something stops them, lighting every lantern in the bay, one new rule at a time.

experiments.title: Stillspring
experiments.idea: Stillspring: a calm stone-channel puzzle - rotate channel pieces so the spring water reaches the garden

experiments.title: Emberstones
experiments.idea: A ring of standing stones you wake with one thumb: tap a stone and it lights with its neighbours, until every rune in the circle burns.

experiments.title: Moondew
experiments.idea: A moonlit pond: trace a one-thumb trail that wakes every dew drop, one pond puzzle at a time
experiments.verdict: Petter, 19 Nov: "The graphics are very intense and glitchy, the game rules are unclear and don't seem to matter. More structure needed." Revised 20 Nov: the renderer no longer samples the clock for anything that moves (that was the glitch), everything is drawn on whole pixels, the pulses are slower and shallower and the palette is softer; reduced motion now freezes the water entirely. Pond 1 teaches one dew and one line, ponds 2-4 add moss, deep water and currents one at a time, every rule answers a refused step with a shake and its own sound, the goal is a dew count with a clear pond-awake moment, and Undo/Restart buttons join a tappable pond strip behind a new start screen.

experiments.title: Paper Tide
experiments.idea: A paper boat drifting down a rainy night gutter you nudge with one thumb: ripples carry it, leaves and rain answer, and the street quietly changes as you play.

experiments.title: Nightwatch
experiments.idea: A hilltop observatory under a night sky: drag to pan the stars, tap a star to chime it, and constellations quietly name themselves.

experiments.title: Fairy Ring
experiments.idea: A fairy ring of mushrooms in a mossy clearing at dawn, woken with one thumb

experiments.title: Hot Spring
experiments.idea: A pixel-art mountain hot spring at night: a monkey soaks while snow falls, and one thumb stirs the water, parts the steam and wakes what hides in the springs.

experiments.title: Threadloom
experiments.idea: A quiet wooden loom you work with one thumb: drag the shuttle across the warp, tap to beat the weft, and a hidden motif appears when the cloth is finished.

experiments.title: Mosslight Pond
experiments.idea: A pixel-art pond at night you wake with a thumb: ripples call the koi, mossy stones light lanterns, and something pale surfaces when you go still.

experiments.title: Glowworm Hollow
experiments.idea: A dark cave of glow-worms you wake with a thumb: tap, drag, hold and swipe the rock, and their light reveals what it hides.

experiments.title: Lantern Alley
experiments.idea: A lantern-lit pixel alley you walk with one thumb, warming lanterns and finding three lost coins.

experiments.title: Snow Garden
experiments.idea: A quiet snowy garden: a tap sends a small walker trudging through the snow, footprints fill in slowly, and a fox crosses if you stand still.
experiments.verdict: 10 Nov: liked it, and asked for more interaction. Added a drag that draws a groove in the snow, a tap on the tree that shakes snow off and moves the bird to the gate, a long press that rolls a snowball into a snowman (three at most, tap one to topple it), and a swipe across the sky that thickens the fall for a few seconds. Pending re-review.

experiments.title: Low Tide
experiments.idea: A pixel-art low-tide rock shore: every tap blooms a soft wave over a pool and gently wakes what lives in it.

experiments.title: Dune Drift
experiments.idea: A quiet moonlit dune field: tap and a handful of sand drifts down and settles softly into the dunes.
experiments.verdict: pending review (revision: landscape seeded per visit with ?seed= override, terrain now seed-driven)

experiments.title: Songbranch
experiments.idea: A pixel-art dusk tree you nudge: tap a bird and it flutters in place and answers, the scene fills the phone, and small secrets hide in the moon, the nest and the leaves.
experiments.verdict: revised 7 Nov (gentler birds, full screen mobile, secrets); pending review

experiments.title: Lantern Moss
experiments.idea: A calm pixel-art clearing you explore with one thumb: gather three lost lights and wake an old stone.
experiments.verdict: Liked a lot, together with Koi Drift. Keep the pixel art. Next: combine the two, with taps that feel impactful and still calm.

experiments.title: Koi Drift
experiments.idea: A still pond you feed with one thumb: tap and food drifts down, the koi glide over and the ripples spread and fade.
experiments.verdict: Liked a lot, together with Lantern Moss. Keep the pond and the koi.

experiments.title: Fireflies
experiments.idea: A dusk meadow you fill with fireflies: one tap lifts a small hush of them, and they drift, blink and slowly fade.
experiments.verdict: Liked a lot, very nice. More like this.

experiments.title: Zen Rake
experiments.idea: A zen sand garden you rake with one thumb; grooves settle behind the rake and slowly fade.
experiments.verdict: Underwhelming: the raking feels harsh, not relaxing. It needs more satisfying physics (sand that gives, settles and smooths softly).

experiments.title: Ripple Pool
experiments.idea: A calm, one-handed tap-to-ripple pond with soft audio.
experiments.verdict: Great start. Wanted more ripples per stone, moving slower, and each impact dissipating gradually. Petter's idea for a next night: a zen garden raking experience.
